text:
deploy-bot: 🚨 Release 2026.3.14 candidate blocked by policy check
```
check: license-scan
status: FAIL
reason: transitive dependency 'libcrypto-2.1.0' has incompatible license (GPL-3.0) detected in layer pkgs/openssl
action: blocked by default policy 'no-gpl-transitive'
```
kayla: ugh, this is from the new grpc client bump. I can see it in the SBOM.
mike: can we confirm it's truly pulled into the runtime? might be dev-only?
sam: I grep'd the image: vendor/grpc/proto -> openssl dep shows up in final image. looks like it's included in the wheel.
legal: FYI we can't accept GPL-3 at runtime for hosted customers. need a plan: remove, replace, or get explicit exception.
kayla: options: 1) revert the grpc bump (quick) 2) patch dependency to MIT variant (risky) 3) request legal exception for this specific package until we ship a non-GPL fix.
sre-bot: note: change window for next minor release opens in 48h. any exception must be timeboxed and audited.
mike: if revert is straightforward, that's least risky for canary. how big is the change?
kayla: it's a one-line upgrade bump in requirements.txt but there are generated code changes. revert might break some integration tests.
product: need to know customer-facing impact. can we ship a patch release without the feature?
sam: feature is optional for the rollout. can disable flag at build time to avoid pulling the new grpc code.
legal: if we go exception route, require: detailed SBOM entry, risk assessment, and explicit end-of-life date for the exception. also sign-off from security and product.
kayla: proposed immediate plan: temporarily disable new-grpc feature flag in the build to remove the transitive GPL dep, proceed with canary. open a follow-up ticket to either replace or vendor a permissive fork within 2 weeks.
mike: +1 for disable-flag -> canary. low blast radius.
product: agree. update release notes with note: "feature deferred due to third-party license change" — keep messaging transparent.
sre-bot: deploybot: mark release candidate as HOLD->EXEMPTION with tag temp-license-exception?
deploy-bot: action recorded: release 2026.3.14 marked HOLD. exemption request created: EX-2026-0314-01. awaiting legal & security sign-off.
legal: I'll review the SBOM diff and the risk memo. target response within 4 business hours.
kayla: I'll prep the SBOM snippet and the rebuild recipe now, pinging here when ready.
sam: I can run an isolated build with the feature flag off and push a canary image to staging registry.
product: once legal signs off, I want the changelog entry and customer comms drafted before canary.
mike: assigning myself to test the canary and smoke tests once image is up.
kayla: thanks team. will post the SBOM snippet in ~20m. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: reminder: automatic escalate to oncall after 12h if unresolved.
